article_title: Analysis of Student Behaviour in Habitable Worlds Using Continuous Representation Visualization
citation: Pardos, Z. A., & Horodyskyj, L. (2018). Analysis of Student Behaviour in Habitable Worlds Using Continuous Representation Visualization. https://github.com/CAHLR/d3-scatterplot
title: d3-scatterplot open-source visualization tool
description: An interactive, in-house d3-based visualization developed alongside the research to let the subject matter expert inspect plots by hovering over points to reveal semantic meta-information such as the question name and lesson, with a colouring feature for categorical attributes like lesson. The article notes its features were similar to the commercial package Tableau but that it "is now open sourced to the community," with the benefit of being easily linked via URL in shared web documents. It served as the inspection interface for the skip-gram/t-SNE visualizations in the Habitable Worlds case study.
requirements: A browser-based d3 environment; the tool is hosted and shared via URL links in web documents
target_learners: online higher education students (whose data the tool visualizes)
target_learning_goals: instructor analysis of student behaviour to improve course design
examples: Used by the course instructor to inspect the highest-rated visualization with annotations, hovering over plot points to reveal element metadata
key_sources: Pardos, Z. A., & Horodyskyj, L. (2018). Analysis of Student Behaviour in Habitable Worlds Using Continuous Representation Visualization. https://github.com/CAHLR/d3-scatterplot
